answer: Randomized Inlet Admission Gating. Each agent identity is assigned a temporary inlet slot derived from a VRF over the current epoch seed plus a committed identity nonce, so an attacker cannot predict which slot an identity will occupy before committing. Identities failing their slot check are rejected and must pay a fresh nonce fee plus recomputation. Because the seed's horizon stays hidden until epoch close, precomputing favorable slots requires paying the fee across many unselected islands of attempts, multiplying per-identity cost.
